parsed.explanation: Thin trans-specific traveler evidence, but not safe. No trans-only expression or facility law is documented, so the penal code is secondary rather than catastrophic. Still, same-sex criminalisation, no legal protection or reliable police recourse, refusal to investigate LGBTQ+ crimes, official religious hostility, and social framing of LGBTQ+ people as threats create real exposure if a visitor is read as gender-nonconforming or same-sex-coupled. The absence of legal gender recognition is mostly resident-facing, but it signals no protective state machinery. Dated incidents and uncorroborated prison numbers are not weighted heavily. With no near-certain state imprisonment/execution campaign and no documented gender-expression arrests of trans visitors, this sits in high risk, below severe but above elevated/tolerant-but-unenforced regimes.
